headline: Bohm powers Phillies past Cardinals in 10th, 7-6
recap: The Phillies beat the Cardinals 7-6 in 10 innings on Friday night at Citizens Bank Park. St. Louis led 2-0 after Jordan Walker's two-run homer in the first, but Philadelphia answered with two runs in the second and one in the third to go ahead. Joshua Baez's two-run homer put the Cardinals back in front in the sixth, but the Phillies scored twice in the bottom of the inning to retake the lead, 5-4. St. Louis tied it again in the eighth on an unearned run off Orion Kerkering. In the 10th, the Cardinals scored an unearned run off Alex McFarlane to lead 6-5, but Philadelphia answered with two runs in the bottom of the inning to win it. Alec Bohm went 3-for-5 with a triple and three RBIs, J.T. Realmuto had two doubles and two RBIs, and Brandon Marsh added two hits and an RBI. Jesus Luzardo struck out nine over 5.2 innings in the start. McFarlane (2-1) got the win; Luis Gastelum (3-3) took the loss.
The win extended the Phillies' winning streak to seven games. Philadelphia is 71-58, in second place in the NL East, four games behind the first-place Braves.

The Phillies continue their series with the Cardinals tonight at Citizens Bank Park, with first pitch at 6:05 PM ET. Andrew Painter is scheduled to start for Philadelphia; St. Louis has not announced a starter. Philadelphia is a -129 moneyline favorite, with St. Louis at +120.
